workshops.title: Swift 6 lab: check shared values, cancellation, and ownership
workshops.summary: Predict compiler messages, run controlled clock and channel checks, and trace who owns a value. Use the results to explain one migration decision.

simple.story: A repair shop has one tool case marked 3 and one person responsible for it. A visitor may open the case, read its label, and close it. Responsibility stays with the owner. For final disposal, the owner records the number 3 and hands the case to the disposal desk. The recorded number remains useful. The old ownership ticket does not: it cannot be used to borrow that case again. Reading the label and giving up the right to use the case are different actions.
simple.meaning: OwnedInt holds one allocated integer. Its borrowing read leaves the owner usable. Its consuming extract returns an Int and consumes the owner binding. The returned value can remain usable after the storage owner is destroyed. Swift checks invalid reuse of that binding.

example.before: A synthetic owner is created as OwnedInt(3). A borrowing read returns 3, and the owner can still be used.
example.change: Call the owner's consuming extract method and keep the returned Int as result.
example.after: result is 3. The old owner binding cannot be read again; the compiler rejects that reuse. The copied integer does not need the owner's pointer to remain allocated.

picture.caption: Borrowing preserves the owner; consuming extraction ends use of the old binding.

items.label: Owner holds 3
items.text: One noncopyable owner manages one initialized integer slot.

items.label: Borrow to read
items.text: Reading returns 3 while leaving the owner usable.

items.label: Consume to extract
items.text: Extraction returns 3 and consumes this owner binding.

items.label: Keep the value
items.text: The returned Int is usable, but the old binding cannot be reused.

words.meaning: Using a value temporarily without consuming its owner.
Using a value so the caller cannot use that binding afterward.
A type whose values Swift does not allow you to copy.
A transfer contract that allows a value to cross an isolation boundary when the old domain gives up conflicting access.
An owner that isolates access to its mutable state; it does not have a dedicated thread.
A request that work should stop; acceptance, cleanup, and already completed effects still need rules.

simple.remember: A borrowed read leaves the owner available; a consuming use ends use of that binding.
simple.boundary: The case story explains ownership, not thread scheduling. Noncopyable does not make every pointer access safe. sending follows a separate rule for crossing isolation boundaries and does not promise a deep copy. For repeating callbacks, stop registration and wait until callbacks can no longer run before releasing their context. Cancellation alone does not make that release safe.

sections.title: Write down what each compiler check should show
sections.html:
A migration audit checks what a proposed language or settings change would affect. This lab gives you small programs whose outcomes you can predict and inspect. Work in a scratch copy of ConcurrencyMigrationLab. It has no remote package dependencies, account fixtures, or native app target. Predict which compiler cases pass, warn, or fail. Record the compiler version, language mode, module isolation default, upcoming feature flags, deployment assumptions, and exit status. Isolation describes which execution domain may access a value. A rejected unsafe program counts as a successful negative check only when the compiler rejects the intended mistake.

The package requires a Swift 6.2+ toolchain, Swift 6 language mode and macOS 15+ for its Synchronization-based manual clock. It explicitly chooses nonisolated default inference. The author verified it on Apple Swift 6.4; that establishes current local behavior, not identical behavior on an untested 6.2 compiler. If your compiler is older, the diagnostic runner reports a skip rather than calling missing-feature errors a successful migration. Do not edit a company target to make the exercise runnable.

Run sh verify-host.sh and python3 verify-diagnostics.py from the lab directory. An evidence ledger is simply a record of what you ran and what you observed. Both place outputs and caches in fresh unique /private/tmp directories. The host script records the toolchain and Swift Testing output; the diagnostic script preserves each stderr log, command and status in results.json. Keep the printed evidence paths in your own submission. These files are scratch evidence, not bundled learner completion records. The lab README records the author's actual checks and limits.

sections.title: Change one compiler setting at a time
sections.html:
Concurrency checking asks whether code can safely use values across isolation boundaries. Start with MutableGlobal.swift, which has a mutable global with no owner controlling access. Predict a warning in Swift 5 with complete checking and an error in Swift 6. The warning build can succeed while the program remains unsafe. Changing language mode does not create an actor. Write one repair for a synthetic UI counter and another for an account cache. Their owners can differ even when their diagnostics both mention shared state.

Default isolation is the rule applied to declarations that do not state their own isolation. DefaultIsolation.swift checks that setting separately. An unannotated free function returns an integer and an explicitly nonisolated function calls it. It passes with a nonisolated module default and fails when that free function becomes MainActor-isolated. Imported code is not rewritten by this setting. Compare this module-local rule with the real client helper's selective SWIFT_VERSION declaration, which is read-only source evidence rather than a resolved compile invocation.

CallerIsolation.swift checks where an async call runs: a mutable worker held by an actor is called through an ordinary nonisolated async method. Without NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault the cross-domain call is rejected; with it the example passes. ConcurrentBoundary.swift explicitly leaves the actor and remains rejected. Explain why this can protect race safety while exposing a UI responsiveness risk for synchronous parsing. Kotlin dispatcher vocabulary motivates deliberate execution policy but does not promise Swift's exact executor scheduling.

Finish with a proposal that names the module owner, affected code, dependent callers, and settings to restore if the change fails. Do not merge MainActor defaults, Swift 6 enforcement and caller execution into one unreviewable preference. A device recording plan belongs in the evidence ledger as pending until actually performed.

sections.title: Follow transferred values, task metadata, and clock steps
sections.html:
A sending parameter lets a value cross an isolation boundary under a transfer rule. Transfer.swift hands a fresh mutable reference to an actor. The positive branch does not use it afterward from the source. INVALID reads the same region after transfer and must be rejected. A region is a group of values connected by aliases that the compiler tracks together. In Contracts.swift, the actor returns only a String snapshot. Explain why transfer is neither permanent Sendable conformance nor a deep copy. Then inspect Conformance.swift: Caption use in its allowed domain succeeds, while a concurrent generic consumer of its isolated conformance is rejected.

Task-local context is metadata bound to a task's execution scope, such as a trace label. It follows different rules from ownership transfer. Predict that an async-let child and ordinary Task inherit the synthetic trace while Task.detached sees nil. The host test joins all handles and checks nested binding restoration. Inheriting metadata does not make an unstructured task a structured child or establish parent cancellation. Compare it to Kotlin CoroutineContext without relabeling it Java ThreadLocal. For detached work requiring correlation, define an explicit permitted value and binding, along with an independent task owner.

An injected clock lets a test control time. Inspect delayed(using:delay:) and ManualClock. Await the registration barrier before advancing virtual time. Four of five seconds keeps one pending sleep; the final second produces ready. Cancellation removes a registered sleeper; later advancement must not resume it twice. The fake clock ignores tolerance, advances only forward and does not model operating-system wakeup jitter. Those limitations are appropriate for a deadline contract test and insufficient for battery or native background claims.

sections.title: Check when a channel accepts or cancels a value
sections.html:
A channel hands values from a sender to a receiver. DemandChannel accepts no buffered values. It retains at most one proposal while its sender is blocked. next asks for one element. When sender and receiver match, the actor removes pending state before resuming either continuation. That acceptance decision happens within one uninterrupted actor execution segment; the actor does not need a dedicated thread. Another blocked producer or consumer is rejected. This is a deliberately small API. It does not implement a complete AsyncSequence or AsyncAlgorithms channel.

Read the producer-first and consumer-first tests to see both registration directions. Then inspect cancellation after registration: canceled sender data must disappear before a replacement is received, and a canceled receiver must not consume a later value. The pre-registration test cancels its own current task before entry and expects immediate rejection. A separate match-wins test receives first, then cancels the sender, and still joins the accepted send successfully. It documents a legal ordering rather than using sleeps to force a fragile race.

Calling finish closes this channel: a blocked producer receives closed and a blocked receiver receives nil. Calling it twice does not resume either continuation twice. New sends fail. The test-only registration observers require a schedule that actually produces the event; they are not cancellation-aware production wait APIs. A consumer leaving early needs an explicit finish-and-join path or the producer can stay suspended indefinitely.

The official AsyncAlgorithms guide supplies broader channel semantics and a nonthrowing send operation. Cancellation and termination can unblock that send without delivering a command. A receipt acknowledgment says the value was received. Neither that API nor this local receipt proves that processing or a durable save completed. Bound producers and payloads; if durable processing matters, add a separate bounded acknowledgment with request identity and failure recovery. Do not claim a global memory bound by counting accepted buffer slots alone.

sections.title: Track each allocation, borrowed use, and final release
sections.html:
An allocation reserves storage. Initialization puts valid values into it. Destruction ends those values, and deallocation returns the storage. Find these separate steps in scopedSum, OwnedInt, and retainedRoundTrip in Contracts.swift. scopedSum initializes two slots to four, returns eight, and uses defer for destruction and deallocation. OwnedInt offers a borrowed read and consuming extraction. The returned integer can outlive the allocation; the consumed owner binding cannot be read again. Ownership.swift checks both a valid compile and rejection of invalid reuse.

Exclusivity means overlapping accesses must obey Swift's access rules. Exclusivity.swift rejects two inout arguments that refer to the same local variable. That rule matters on one thread and is distinct from actor isolation. A pointer can bypass some checks while remaining invalid; it is not an exception that makes shared memory safe. No dangling-pointer run is provided. Native C allocation must be freed by its documented allocator family, and a pointer borrowed from a withUnsafe closure must not escape its scope.

Unmanaged lets code account for retains outside ordinary automatic ownership. This synchronous sample takes one retained context back into managed ownership exactly once and checks a weak observation after scope. Describe a repeating callback separately: registration owns one retain, callbacks borrow it, unregister must acknowledge callback quiescence, and one terminal path releases it. The sample does not execute that native registration or prove vendor callback behavior. Cancellation is not immediate deallocation and deinit cannot await unregister. Java AutoCloseable and Kotlin use help explain cleanup while allowing different aliasing behavior.

exercise.brief: Write your own migration audit. Include compiler predictions, observed host results, and one decision about cancellation and ownership.
steps: Predict the result and diagnostic reason for all fourteen compiler cases. Then run the verifier and compare.
Run the host checks and save their printed evidence path. Explain the state boundary each check covers, rather than how long it took.
Make a table separating warning/error enforcement, default isolation, caller execution, transfer, conformance, consumed reuse, and aliasing.
For a synthetic command that must be saved, decide whether the caller needs receipt or completed-processing acknowledgment. Explain why.
List who retains, borrows, unregisters, and releases a repeating callback context. Mark native target work that you have not checked.
acceptance: Fourteen diagnostic cases match expected success/failure and category on a supported compiler.
All thirteen host tests pass without elapsed-time sleeps.
The report separates clock/context/channel contracts from legacy stale-result tests.
Receipt, cancellation, ordinary failure and shutdown have explicit meanings.
The callback ledger has one final release after quiescence and no escaped temporary pointer.
No production migration, simulator execution, sanitizer result or learner certification is asserted.
exercise.solution:
Begin with your actual toolchain and settings. Pair each prediction with its log. The mutable-global cases check warning versus error enforcement. The default-isolation cases check the module's inferred isolation. Ordinary-worker off/on and explicit-concurrent rejection check execution boundaries. The transfer pair checks valid transfer and rejected source reuse. The conformance pair checks where a protocol implementation may be used. The ownership pair checks valid use and rejected reuse after consumption. The inout case checks overlapping access to one variable. These are separate rules. If your compiler lacks a required feature, record a skip to resolve. An unrelated failure does not establish the intended contract.

The host answer follows registered events rather than wall-clock scheduling. Receive one proposed value and join its sender, cancel registered sender/receiver independently before replacement, close each type of waiter, and reject overlapping blocked operations. The newly added schedules check canceled entry and accepted match before late cancellation. For time, advance a registered five-second sleep by four plus one and cancel another; for context, join inherited and detached observations and check restoration. For transfer, ask only for the actor's snapshot. For ownership, verify bounded values and the local retain round trip.

For a persisted command, choose explicit processing acknowledgment keyed by a synthetic command ID. A receipt only proves the consumer obtained the value, and a terminal channel wakeup may not prove even that under the library API. The owner resolves acknowledgment with committed, ordinary failure or canceled according to a documented transaction policy and bounds outstanding entries. On early consumer exit it finishes the channel and joins the producer. For repeating callbacks, retain at registration, borrow per callback, acknowledge quiescence, then release once. Device responsiveness, native callback implementation, sanitizer evidence and supported older compiler runs stay pending. The learner's submission needs its own predictions and evidence; this worked path does not record completion.

quiz.question: The INVALID consumed-value fixture fails because its syntax is unknown on an older compiler. Is that expected evidence?
options: Yes, any failure proves the contract.
No; the supported compiler and expected diagnostic category must match.
Yes, because failed compilation is device testing.
quiz.explanation: A missing feature is an availability gap. The runner gates compiler version and checks the specific contract diagnostic rather than accepting arbitrary failure.

quiz.question: A channel matched an element, then the sender was canceled. What does the local contract permit?
options: Retraction after the consumer received it.
Successful receipt remains accepted; later processing has its own policy.
quiz.explanation: Match removes the pending sender before resume. A later cancellation cannot undo receipt; it may still affect separately owned processing.

quiz.question: Which evidence does retainedRoundTrip provide?
options: A bounded synchronous retain balance and weak lifetime observation.
Quiescence of every native repeating callback.
Proof that the opaque pointer is Sendable.
quiz.explanation: The host sample is synchronous and one-shot. Native callback cardinality, unregister behavior and concurrency safety require separate target evidence.
